column4: mu = muhat / (1 + K_s/S + S/K_i)

K_s = saturation constant, numerically equals lowest concentration of substrate at which the specific growth rate is equal to one-half the maximum specific growth rate in the absence of inhibition, mass/volume

column4: In the usual continuous culture, operated near steady state, substrate concentrations are low and the term S/K_i is therefore much less than the term K_s/S even for low values of K_i. Under these conditions the inhibition function reduces to the Monod function.

Analytical solutions of the nonlinear differential equations representing the dynamic behaviour of microbial systems are usually unavailable. However, these equations can be solved using the analog computer or one of the digital-analog simulation programs. The solutions presented in this paper were obtained using PACTOLUS on the IBM 360 computer.
